correctness.rationale: On the entire domain \(0<y\le x\le1\), sorting the exact child triples gives three L and two R chambers. Direct inequalities show \(L^2(\mathcal T)\subseteq F\) and \(R(\mathcal T)\subseteq G\), and invariance of F,G. In F the physical middle angle is conserved, in G the smallest is conserved, and the largest angle satisfies \(a_{n+1}=S-a_n/2\). Solving this proves every pointwise limit and the alternating factor \((-1/2)^n\). Composition at at most two/one transient steps yields the displayed four/two chamber formulas. Rational witnesses (1/10,1/10), (4/5,3/5), (3/4,1/4) prove sharpness. The standalone checker independently implements sorted-angle child maps and passed 743 exact-rational initial states, checking iterates through n=12; infinite validity rests on explicit proof, not tests.

value.rationale: The motivating complete symbolic classification singles out pure itineraries as the only exceptional regime, yet leaves their final shape undetermined. This theorem gives a natural full-domain classification of those exceptional limits, explicitly enumerating four left and two right initial chambers, universal finite transients, and a sharp oscillatory spectral rate; any eventually pure itinerary is then exactly computable after its finite prefix. These are structural dynamical invariants, not arbitrary numerical slices, and sharpen qualitative set attraction to pointwise geometry. No downstream theorem is required for the intrinsic classification value.
